# wt — Command & Function Index

A generated index of every `wt` command and every public function, with a one-line
purpose each. Regenerate with `scripts/gen-docs.sh --write`; CI fails on drift.

## Commands

The command surface, from `wt.sh`'s dispatch. Run `wt <command> --help` for full usage.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `wt c, create` | Parse `wt create` flags, resolve the branch name (Linear ID / plain / scratch), and delegate to the core worker. |
| `wt o, open` | Locate a worktree (by query or fzf picker) and open it in cmux/tmux/shell. |
| `wt ls` | List worktrees across every project, annotating each with live PR status. |
| `wt rm` | Parse `wt delete` flags and delete one worktree (or route to the interactive picker), tearing down services, tmux, slot, state, and branch. |
| `wt prune` | Parse `wt delete` flags and delete one worktree (or route to the interactive picker), tearing down services, tmux, slot, state, and branch. |
| `wt code, cursor` | Locate a worktree (from cwd, arg, or fzf picker) and open it in the resolved editor. |
| `wt pr` | Route `wt pr` to browser-open (default) or the conflicts subcommand. |
| `wt delete` | Parse `wt delete` flags and delete one worktree (or route to the interactive picker), tearing down services, tmux, slot, state, and branch. |
| `wt list` | List one project's worktrees (table or JSON), pruning stale entries first. |
| `wt start, up` | Start a worktree's services in the current terminal (or the main repo root as slot 0). |
| `wt stop, down` | Stop a worktree's services (or the main repo root's); with no service names, stops all. |
| `wt status, st` | Show a worktree's git state, ports, and DB connection details. |
| `wt attach, a` | Attach the terminal to a worktree's tmux session, creating the window if it is missing. |
| `wt run` | Run a single named setup step in a worktree, with ports/env exported. |
| `wt exec` | Execute an arbitrary command in a worktree's directory with ports/env exported. |
| `wt init` | Scaffold a wt project config for the current git repo. |
| `wt config` | View, edit, or print the path of a global or project wt config. |
| `wt ports` | Show a worktree's port assignments, overrides, availability, and DB connection. |
| `wt send, s` | Send a command string to a service/pane of a worktree's tmux window. |
| `wt logs, log` | Capture and print recent tmux pane output for a worktree (default pane 0, a named target, or all panes). |
| `wt panes` | List a worktree window's tmux panes as a table (service/command, active, size). |
| `wt doctor, doc` | Run all diagnostic checks (deps, config, state, tmux, ports) and print a health report. |
| `wt db` | Route `wt db <subcommand>` to the matching handler (reset / url / dump / use-remote / detach). |

### `lib/config.sh`

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ensure_yq` | Ensure yq is installed, aborting otherwise. |
| `init_config_dirs` | Create the wt config, projects, data, state, and log directories. |

| `project_config_path` | Print the config file path for a project. |
| `has_global_config` | Test whether the global config file exists. |
| `has_project_config` | Test whether a project's config file exists. |
| `yaml_get` | Read a single YAML value with yq, falling back to a default. |
| `yaml_array` | Read a YAML array, one element per line. |
| `yaml_array_length` | Count the elements of a YAML array. |
| `yaml_set` | Write a string YAML value, creating the file if needed. |
| `yaml_set_num` | Write a numeric YAML value, creating the file if needed. |
| `yaml_delete` | Delete a YAML path from a file if the file exists. |
| `require_project` | Return the given project name, or auto-detect it from the cwd. |
| `detect_project` | Detect the project for the current directory by repo root or configured repo_path. |
| `load_project_config` | Load a project's config into PROJECT_* globals and validate its port ranges. |
| `get_setup_steps` | Count the configured setup steps. |
| `get_setup_step` | Read one field of a setup step by index. |
| `get_services` | Count the configured services. |

| `resolve_db_url` | Resolve the worktree's DB URL from its env file, else the config template. |
| `redact_db_url` | Mask the password in a postgres URL for display: user:pass@host -> user:****@host. |
| `parse_db_url` | Parse a postgres URL into its components for display. |
| `list_projects` | List all configured project names. |

### `lib/context.sh`

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `resolve_worktree_context` | Resolve project + worktree path/slot for a command operating on one existing worktree. |
| `export_worktree_env` | Export ports + env for the resolved context; call after resolve_worktree_context. |
| `resolve_tmux_context` | Resolve project + the tmux session/window for a command inspecting a worktree window. |

### `lib/port.sh`

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `calculate_dynamic_port` | Calculate a dynamic port by hashing the branch name (cksum: deterministic, portable). |
| `calculate_reserved_port` | Calculate a slot's reserved port: base + slot*services_per_slot + offset (slot 0 -> 3000/3001, slot 1 -> 3002/3003, …). |
| `calculate_worktree_ports` | Compute every service port for a worktree — reserved (slot-derived, or .ports.main.<svc> under WT_MAIN_CONTEXT) plus dynamic (hashed, collision-avoided). |
| `export_port_vars` | Export PORT_<SERVICE> env vars for every service (project overrides applied when given). |
| `get_service_port` | Get the port for one service (checks project overrides first when project given). |
| `slots_file` | Print the path to the slot-assignments file. |
| `init_slots_file` | Create the slots file with an empty slots map if it does not already exist. |
| `get_slot_for_worktree` | Look up the slot already assigned to a worktree. |
| `claim_slot` | Claim a slot for a worktree under a file lock (idempotent if already assigned). |
| `release_slot` | Release the slot a worktree holds, under a file lock. |
| `list_slots` | List every slot assignment for a project. |
| `slots_in_use` | Count how many slots a project currently holds. |
| `is_port_available` | Report whether a port is free, via exit status. |
| `find_available_port` | Find a free port in a range, trying a preferred port first. |

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|

| `setup_services_top_2_layout_window` | Apply the services-top-2 layout to a worktree window (delegates with win_idx=0). |
| `configure_window_panes` | Send cd + service/command keystrokes into each pane of a window. |
| `setup_services_top_layout` | Arrange a window as the services-top layout: services on top, main panes below. |
| `setup_services_top_2_layout` | Arrange a window as the services-top-2 layout: 2 services on top, 2 command panes below. |
| `kill_session` | Kill the worktree's tmux window (leaves the session intact). |

| `list_sessions` | List the window names in the main tmux session. |
| `send_to_pane` | Send a command line (followed by Enter) to a specific pane. |
| `find_service_pane` | Locate the window:pane hosting a given service from config. |
| `create_service_window` | Create a dedicated tmux window for a service (idempotent). |
| `session_info` | Print each window's index, name, and active flag for a session. |
| `capture_pane` | Capture the recent scrollback text of a pane. |
| `list_window_panes` | List each pane in a window with its format info. |
| `interrupt_pane` | Send an interrupt (Ctrl+C) to a pane or window. |

| `expand_path` | Expand a leading ~ to $HOME in a path. |

| `port_in_use` | Report whether a TCP port has a listener (predicate). |
| `print_kv` | Print an aligned bold key-value pair. |
